status: Specifications only; these scenarios have not been executed.

scenarios.title: M8 baseline does not become completion evidence
scenarios.given: The prior plan and 75 scenario definitions exist but execution reports do not.
expected: All implementation gates remain unverified; IDs and expected behavior are preserved.

scenarios.title: Stable identity survives folder moves
scenarios.given: A resource and generated operations have stable semantic IDs.
scenarios.when: Move declarations between folders without changing explicit module identity.
expected: Wire/security identities and migration plan remain unchanged.

scenarios.title: Deterministic build under discovery variation
scenarios.given: Identical inputs and lockfile are compiled in isolated directories.
scenarios.when: Shuffle file discovery order and absolute filesystem paths.
expected: Canonical artifacts and semantic digests match.

scenarios.title: Document edit has bounded digest impact
scenarios.given: Only a field description changes.
scenarios.when: Compute wire, governance-effect and documentation digests.
expected: Documentation changes; execution privileges do not widen or require needless reapproval.

scenarios.title: Security-only change affects security digest
scenarios.given: Add an external effect without changing function I/O.
expected: Security/effect digest changes and review is required.

scenarios.title: Unknown critical IR extension fails closed
scenarios.given: An imported IR uses an unknown critical capability operator.
expected: Compilation rejects it rather than dropping the operator.

scenarios.title: No execution during contract import
scenarios.given: An imported package includes an executable install script.
expected: Only allowed contract bytes are read; no script or network code runs.

scenarios.title: Edition compatibility is explicit
scenarios.given: A supported M8 artifact and unsupported future artifact are available.
scenarios.when: Load both through the next compiler.
expected: M8 is converted by a specified rule; unsupported future semantics produce a diagnostic.

scenarios.title: Original target refactor preserves behavior
scenarios.given: Existing M8 application is bound through compatibility shims.
scenarios.when: Run the original client and all applicable baseline scenarios.
expected: No unexplained wire, state or error change occurs.

scenarios.title: Postgres unique-create race
scenarios.given: Two commands create the same tenant-scoped unique code.
expected: One commits; the loser has a typed conflict and no success outbox/audit.

scenarios.title: Postgres reference deletion race
scenarios.given: A child creation races with deletion of its parent.
scenarios.when: Run both under the generated guard protocol.
expected: No committed dangling reference is possible.

scenarios.title: SQL facade parity
scenarios.given: Identical plans run through Drizzle and Effect SQL.
scenarios.when: Inject failure after guarded update but before completion.
expected: Either all committed effects exist or none; facade selection does not change results.

scenarios.title: Pooled authorization context isolation
scenarios.given: Tenant A and B reuse the same PostgreSQL pool connection.
scenarios.when: Interleave successful, failing and cancelled transactions.
expected: B cannot inherit A tenant/RLS/session authority.

scenarios.title: Connection-mode capability rejection
scenarios.given: A selected HTTP driver cannot support a required interactive transaction.
expected: Planner rejects it or chooses an explicitly approved equivalent plan.

scenarios.title: Authorization query cache bypass
scenarios.given: A role or subject restriction changes at origin.
scenarios.when: Read through the selected Hyperdrive connection.
expected: Authorization queries use the certified noncached path and respect the declared revocation bound.

scenarios.title: Node shutdown and retry recovery
scenarios.given: A Node worker is terminated around message processing.
expected: No acknowledged job disappears and no business mutation duplicates.

scenarios.title: Multilabel taxonomy inheritance
scenarios.given: A custom type inherits contact and identifier classifications.
expected: All applicable ancestors are preserved; unknown labels do not become public.

scenarios.title: Organization versus natural-person subject
scenarios.given: Customer is an organization; Contact is a person.
expected: Customer ownership alone does not identify an erasure subject; concrete Contact links do.

scenarios.title: Shared guardian subject
scenarios.given: Two students reference one guardian contact.
scenarios.when: Locate data for the first student.
expected: Guardian linkage and other student interests are reported; no indiscriminate cascade is proposed.

scenarios.title: Hidden filter contributes lineage
scenarios.given: A view returns names but filters on a health field.
expected: Health processing remains in lineage despite not appearing in output columns.

scenarios.title: Raw network escape loses coverage
scenarios.given: A handwritten function uses a raw HTTP client outside declared capabilities.
scenarios.when: Analyze its declared effects and coverage.
expected: The system records unmodeled/unchecked effects rather than a complete flow proof.

scenarios.title: Detector failure cannot declassify
scenarios.given: A declared-sensitive blob inspection times out.
expected: It remains restricted/pending review, never public because nothing was detected.

scenarios.title: Pseudonym remains linkable
scenarios.given: A subject identifier is replaced with a stable keyed hash.
expected: Linkability and retention requirements remain unless a separate justified assessment establishes otherwise.

scenarios.title: Nonpersonal industrial sensitivity
scenarios.given: A recipe contains a proprietary formula and safety threshold but no people.
expected: Confidentiality/integrity controls apply without labeling every field personal data.

scenarios.title: Purpose hierarchy grants nothing
scenarios.given: A child purpose extends a parent with a readable Contact surface.
scenarios.when: Request Contact under the child without a surface mapping.
expected: No implicit access is granted.

scenarios.title: Sticky deny survives another include
scenarios.given: A fragment denies supportNotes; another fragment allows them.
scenarios.when: Compose in both orders and flatten.
expected: supportNotes remains denied; results are order independent.

scenarios.title: Runtime multiple-purpose laundering blocked
scenarios.given: Two separately permitted purposes have different fields.
scenarios.when: Send both labels in invocation metadata seeking their union.
expected: Runtime rejects or chooses an explicitly authorized composite; no ambient union appears.

scenarios.title: Distinct runtime service identities
scenarios.given: Two purpose readers have structurally similar TypeScript interfaces.
scenarios.when: Attempt to satisfy one requirement with the other service key.
expected: Type/service identity verification rejects substitution without an approved mapping.

scenarios.title: Real output minimization
scenarios.given: A storage adapter returns a full record with hidden fields.
scenarios.when: Serialize it through a purpose-scoped reader.
expected: Only approved keys are emitted; a narrowing cast is not treated as redaction.

scenarios.title: Hidden-field query oracle blocked
scenarios.given: An interface omits salary from read fields.
scenarios.when: Try filtering/sorting/counting by salary without query authority.
expected: The request is rejected before query execution.

scenarios.title: Relationship expansion preserves scope
scenarios.given: Order exposes customer identity but not full Customer.Record.
scenarios.when: Request nested Customer with restricted fields.
expected: Expansion requires an approved target surface and row authorization.

scenarios.title: Named action versus generic field write
scenarios.given: An approved reset action changes a server-managed value.
scenarios.when: Invoke the action, then attempt direct PATCH of the value.
expected: The declared action may run under its effect policy; generic field editing remains denied.

scenarios.title: Purpose/tenant/caller spoofing rejected
scenarios.given: An unauthenticated caller supplies forged Forge context headers.
expected: No headers become trusted authority and no protected data is accessed.

scenarios.title: Authorization occurs for every record
scenarios.given: A user can access one student but not another.
scenarios.when: Reuse the same scoped Effect service for two record reads.
expected: The second read denies; constructing a Layer once is not row authorization.

scenarios.title: Candidate-state ownership check
scenarios.given: User can update a current Contact but not assign it to another tenant/customer scope.
expected: Current and candidate state authorization prevents escalation.

scenarios.title: Decision cache policy epoch
scenarios.given: A prior allow is cached under policy epoch N.
scenarios.when: Revoke at epoch N+1 and repeat before cache TTL.
expected: Old cached allow cannot override the new epoch or declared revocation bound.

scenarios.title: Idempotency receipt reauthorization
scenarios.given: A response with personal fields was stored under earlier authority.
scenarios.when: Replay its idempotency key after access is revoked.
expected: Side effects are not repeated and the old sensitive response is not disclosed.

scenarios.title: OPA partial evaluation is bounded
scenarios.given: A policy uses a predicate outside the SQL/filter compiler subset.
expected: It is rejected or given an explicit bounded candidate/residual plan; never an unlimited hidden scan.

scenarios.title: Function identity assurance is honest
scenarios.given: Multiple functions share one process and signing credential.
scenarios.when: Ask to attest isolated caller-function identity.
expected: The profile is rejected/downgraded to workload-bound assurance.

scenarios.title: Mandatory obligation and PIP failure
scenarios.given: A policy decision requires an unknown obligation or missing fresh attribute.
expected: Execution denies rather than ignoring the requirement.

scenarios.title: OpenAPI reference lock and SSRF
scenarios.given: A vendor document includes remote refs and a callback URL to metadata/private hosts.
expected: Only explicitly permitted pinned refs/endpoints are used; forbidden fetches fail.

scenarios.title: OpenAPI serialization and nullability
scenarios.given: A foreign spec uses nullable/optional fields, media/status variants and nontrivial query encoding.
scenarios.when: Round-trip imported operations through test server fixtures.
expected: Canonical mapping preserves meanings or rejects unsupported features.

scenarios.title: External IDs remain foreign
scenarios.given: Vendor customer_id and Forge Customer are both strings.
scenarios.when: Wire them without a reviewed resolver.
expected: Compiler requires semantic mapping rather than accepting structural coincidence.

scenarios.title: Local and remote RPC authorization parity
scenarios.given: The same callable is bound locally and over authenticated HTTP/RPC.
expected: Results and denials match; remote invocation failures remain distinct typed outcomes.

scenarios.title: MCP discovery isolation
scenarios.given: Two identities/purposes see different tools/resources.
scenarios.when: Reuse discovery cache and attempt a hidden operation by name.
expected: Listings remain isolated and direct invocation rechecks authority.

scenarios.title: MCP annotation is not authority
scenarios.given: An unsafe caller supplies/readOnlyHint or altered tool metadata.
expected: The server contract and policy, not client hints, decide execution.

scenarios.title: CLI stable machine contract
scenarios.given: A create/update request comes from flags, JSON file and stdin.
scenarios.when: Run with JSON output and both success/failure.
expected: Canonical input is identical; stdout contains only data, stderr diagnostics, and guarded mutation rules hold.

scenarios.title: Cross-language wire conformance
scenarios.given: Plain TS, Python and Go clients use the same generated surface.
scenarios.when: Exercise decimals, null/absent PATCH, enums, typed errors and jobs.
expected: All match server canonical values; no client requires Effect.

scenarios.title: Digest pin defeats mutable tag
scenarios.given: Registry tag is changed after forge.lock is generated.
expected: The pinned digest is used or resolution fails; the new tag cannot substitute silently.

scenarios.title: Artifact signature and schema verification
scenarios.given: A published artifact has tampered IR or an untrusted signature.
expected: It is not activated or executed.

scenarios.title: Catalog is rebuildable
scenarios.given: Delete the derived catalog index while retaining immutable artifacts.
expected: Equivalent authorized search/graph results return without duplicate semantic versions.

scenarios.title: Catalog metadata confidentiality
scenarios.given: A principal lacks access to a sensitive domain/purpose.
scenarios.when: Search names, graph neighbors and action schemas.
expected: Sensitive metadata is not returned through alternate endpoints.

scenarios.title: Publication not deployment
scenarios.given: A new contract version is published without a release report.
expected: No running service is claimed to implement it.

scenarios.title: Federated identity collision
scenarios.given: Two registries publish the same package name/version.
scenarios.when: Import both under different trust authorities.
expected: Authority-qualified identities remain distinct and grants cannot be reused across them.

scenarios.title: Registry offline bounded behavior
scenarios.given: Runtime holds a valid signed snapshot and registry is unavailable.
scenarios.when: Execute before then after required authority expiry.
expected: Existing operations follow configured offline rules; expiry never turns into indefinite stale permission.

scenarios.title: Discovery endpoint trust
scenarios.given: A valid schema is advertised by an unexpected service endpoint.
scenarios.when: Attempt a remote binding using only its schema hash.
expected: Trusted deployment/audience verification is still required.

scenarios.title: Uses creates request not grant
scenarios.given: Caller adds a new external dependency.
scenarios.when: Publish contract and run request automation.
expected: A pending callee PR exists; runtime access is still denied.

scenarios.title: Idempotent PR automation
scenarios.given: The same caller CI job runs repeatedly.
expected: One request/PR is created or updated, not duplicates.

scenarios.title: Changed PR head invalidates approval
scenarios.given: Caller adds sensitive data after a previous approval.
scenarios.when: Attempt to publish using stale review evidence.
expected: Digest/head mismatch prevents grant activation.

scenarios.title: Multiple reviewer groups enforced
scenarios.given: Payments and Security are both required.
expected: Independent review checks prevent publication until both policies are satisfied.

scenarios.title: Privileged bot isolation
scenarios.given: Caller branch contains executable malicious code and an outside grants path.
expected: Bot never executes caller code and cannot modify unauthorized repositories/paths.

scenarios.title: Nontransitive purpose-bound grant
scenarios.given: A→B and B→C are approved for distinct purposes.
scenarios.when: A attempts C directly or changes purpose on A→B.
expected: The undeclared edge/purpose is denied.

scenarios.title: Merge versus activation
scenarios.given: Callee PR merges but signed grant/snapshot deployment has not completed.
expected: Access remains denied until all activation gates pass.

scenarios.title: Drain and emergency revocation
scenarios.given: Old workflow uses a grant removed from new source.
scenarios.when: Perform planned retirement, then an emergency revoke in a separate run.
expected: Planned removal respects declared drain; emergency revocation applies within its bound and is not undone by rollback.

scenarios.title: Pure diff does not invent live facts
scenarios.given: Diff runs offline with no account/database access.
expected: Report backfill/review need without invented affected-row counts.

scenarios.title: Directional compatibility
scenarios.given: An output enum grows and an input required field is added.
scenarios.when: Compare old/new producer and consumer models.
expected: Reports distinguish exhaustive output clients and old producers; not all additions are labeled compatible.

scenarios.title: Policy comparison uncertainty
scenarios.given: An opaque external Rego bundle changes.
expected: Mark changed/unknown unless a supported proof establishes widening/narrowing.

scenarios.title: Capability narrowing migration
scenarios.given: Remove Contact.email from a purpose while caches/receipts exist.
expected: Old broad cached values are rejected/projected only under current authority before disclosure.

scenarios.title: Fenced deployment resume
scenarios.given: Two controllers race; one loses its lease during backfill.
expected: Only the current controller advances guarded stages; completed actions are not duplicated.

scenarios.title: Rollback cannot restore authority
scenarios.given: An older app version references a revoked grant.
expected: Current revocation remains authoritative.

scenarios.title: Cross-database cutover
scenarios.given: D1 or Dynamo data and blobs are exported under a write fence.
scenarios.when: Import into PostgreSQL and verify before cutover.
expected: IDs/revisions/canonical hashes/invariants match; native workflow history is not fabricated.

scenarios.title: Preview and SLO gate evidence
scenarios.given: Preview contains restricted source data and rollout lacks sufficient traffic/metrics.
expected: Data policy still applies; insufficient telemetry prevents an evidence-based success claim.

scenarios.title: Neon connection profile
scenarios.given: The same Postgres contract uses two driver modes.
expected: Only modes passing the declared semantics are certified.

scenarios.title: PlanetScale exact engine profile
scenarios.given: User selects PlanetScale without an engine/product designation.
expected: Planner requires a known product/engine profile rather than assuming MySQL or PostgreSQL.

scenarios.title: Turso assertion/transaction qualification
scenarios.given: Turso engine/client exposes SQL-compatible syntax.
expected: Syntax compatibility alone cannot pass certification; unsupported guarantees remain rejected.

scenarios.title: Terraform plan equivalence
scenarios.given: One resolved physical plan feeds native IaC and Terraform emitters.
expected: Resources/bindings/ownership satisfy the same requirements without two concurrent state owners.

scenarios.title: Secret-free Docker and Nix artifacts
scenarios.given: Deployment needs database and signing credentials.
scenarios.when: Build image and Nix derivation then inspect artifacts.
expected: Only secret references/config injection paths appear; secret bytes never enter immutable build outputs.

scenarios.title: Self-hosted durable restart
scenarios.given: Node, Postgres and Temporal host Acme.
scenarios.when: Crash API/worker around outbox and external-signal delivery.
expected: Committed state and durable workflow progress recover under the certified protocol.

scenarios.title: Imported resource retention
scenarios.given: Customer supplies an existing database/bucket.
scenarios.when: Destroy a preview or generated stack.
expected: Externally owned authoritative resources are retained unless explicitly approved for destruction.

scenarios.title: Uncertified adapter combination
scenarios.given: User mixes a tested engine with an untested runtime/driver/deployment tuple.
expected: Status is unverified/unsupported, never inherited merely from component names.

scenarios.title: Subject erasure respects other people
scenarios.given: One record contains student and guardian data shared with another student.
scenarios.when: Plan and apply one subject erasure.
expected: Only approved subject-specific data is removed; others and lawful holds are preserved.

scenarios.title: Unknown egress blocks complete claim
scenarios.given: A function has unmodeled exports or an external sink without erasure adapter.
expected: Result reports partial/unknown obligations, not universal completion.

scenarios.title: Delayed event cannot resurrect
scenarios.given: A queued create/update predates a subject deletion epoch.
expected: Suppression prevents recreation under the deleted/restricted subject epoch.

scenarios.title: Restore replays current suppression
scenarios.given: An older database backup contains erased data.
scenarios.when: Restore while using the independently retained current suppression ledger.
expected: Affected records are suppressed/erased before ordinary reads are enabled.

scenarios.title: External acknowledgment is not proof
scenarios.given: Vendor says erasure request accepted but provides no completion confirmation.
expected: External status remains requested/accepted/pending, not verified complete.

scenarios.title: Revocation during export
scenarios.given: A long export is reading chunks and preparing a download.
scenarios.when: Revoke purpose/subject authority before a later chunk or URL issuance.
expected: Further disclosure stops and staged artifacts follow cleanup/retention policy.

scenarios.title: Pseudonymous audit remains protected
scenarios.given: Erasure leaves a keyed subject token in evidence.
scenarios.when: Classify and expose the audit record.
expected: Token remains potentially personal/linkable and access/retention protections remain.

scenarios.title: Recovery claim requires evidence
scenarios.given: Backup configuration exists without recent successful restore evidence.
expected: Report unknown or external evidence required, not proven recovery compliance.

scenarios.title: Sensitive telemetry excluded
scenarios.given: Inputs contain emails, health notes and unbounded customer identifiers.
scenarios.when: Run normal, failed and rejected operations.
expected: Generated logs/metrics/errors/baggage contain only approved metadata, not sensitive values.

scenarios.title: Purpose metadata confidentiality
scenarios.given: Purpose name itself reveals a sensitive process.
expected: Configured handling controls prevent unauthorized disclosure of the sensitive name.

scenarios.title: SLI logical/attempt separation
scenarios.given: One logical operation fails twice then succeeds.
expected: Metrics preserve the intended denominators instead of counting three independent successes/failures as business requests.

scenarios.title: Trace sampling not exact SLO source
scenarios.given: Traces sample a subset and metric export has gaps.
expected: The system does not claim exact counts from traces; gaps and uncertainty are visible.

scenarios.title: Provider metric missing
scenarios.given: A provider lacks a requested metric/OTLP signal path.
expected: Panel is marked missing/unsupported, not healthy zero.

scenarios.title: Evidence signature scope
scenarios.given: Signed evidence says tests ran for a bounded profile/time window.
expected: Report preserves scope, coverage and freshness; signature alone is not universal correctness.

scenarios.title: Observed-edge identity assurance
scenarios.given: A span claims caller FunctionA under shared-workload credentials.
expected: Attribution is qualified by workload-bound assurance, not promoted to cryptographically isolated function identity.

scenarios.title: Unused grant recommendation coverage
scenarios.given: No calls appear in sampled/incomplete telemetry.
expected: It suggests review with coverage limits and does not automatically revoke or claim zero actual use.

scenarios.title: End-to-end surface parity
scenarios.given: Same Acme source and business code run on D1, Dynamo and PostgreSQL.
scenarios.when: Invoke HTTP/MCP/CLI and generated clients under matching contexts.
expected: Equivalent schemas, minimized fields, allowed actions and typed denials are observed.

scenarios.title: Mixed-version security deployment
scenarios.given: Old/new code, schemas, grants and purpose surfaces coexist during rollout.
scenarios.when: Exercise queued old work and new requests with faults.
expected: No old authority bypass or unsupported response reinterpretation occurs.

scenarios.title: Purpose/capability adversarial fuzz
scenarios.given: Random capability DAGs, denials, scoped queries and nested relations are generated.
scenarios.when: Compare compiler outputs with reference algebra and runtime enforcement.
expected: No composition order or traversal path widens effective authority.

scenarios.title: Supply-chain and CI adversarial suite
scenarios.given: Tampered packages, registry responses, overlays and grant artifacts are supplied.
scenarios.when: Build, publish and deploy under restricted CI roles.
expected: No untrusted code execution, credential leakage or unapproved activation occurs.

scenarios.title: Failure evidence honesty
scenarios.given: One required profile/scenario fails or is skipped.
expected: It cannot state all profiles passed; incomplete support is explicit.

scenarios.title: Measured performance profile
scenarios.given: Repeat benchmark workload with baseline and governance enabled.
scenarios.when: Measure cold/warm behavior, PIP latency and write amplification.
expected: Actual per-profile figures and workload limits are recorded without inferred equal latency.

scenarios.title: M8 application upgrade
scenarios.given: Existing source lacks purpose/classification blocks.
expected: No implicit broad governance grants or destructive schema changes occur; old edition status remains explicit.

scenarios.title: Complete reference demo release
scenarios.given: All advertised profiles have recorded gate evidence.
expected: Release lists exact version tuples, supported features, migration requirements and retest/expiry policy.
